messages:
alex: Heads up — ran into a nasty flow where redwoodctl's auto-updater clobbers my active profile while I'm running `redwoodctl localserve`. Local dev server immediately drops auth and prompts to login. super disruptive during iter loops.

alex: Repro (mac/linux, reproduced on both):
1) have active_profile set to 'feature-x' in ~/.config/redwood/active_profile
2) start `redwoodctl localserve --profile feature-x`
3) trigger update check (I saw this automatically after ~30m but you can run `redwoodctl update --check` in another tab)
4) localserve logs: `updater: applying update v1.4.3` then `config: wrote active_profile=default` -> localserve prints `[auth] no credentials for profile 'default', please run redwoodctl login`

alex: Log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-15T09:42:11Z] updater: found new release v1.4.3
[2026-03-15T09:42:13Z] updater: downloading
[2026-03-15T09:42:20Z] updater: applying update
[2026-03-15T09:42:20Z] config: saving default config to ~/.config/redwood/config.json
[2026-03-15T09:42:20Z] config: wrote active_profile=default
[2026-03-15T09:42:20Z] localserve: detected profile change -> reloading auth
[2026-03-15T09:42:20Z] localserve: [auth] no credentials for profile 'default'
```

alex: I'm pretty sure the updater rewrites the config file atomically but with default values, rather than merging with existing user values. I lost session tokens (they were still present in the file earlier) so localserve treated it as no-profile.

sophie: yikes. thanks for the detailed repro. two quick asks: can you paste the full contents of ~/.config/redwood/config.json before/after (sanitized)? that will help decide whether it's a merge bug or an ordering issue.

alex: before (sanitized):
```
{
  "active_profile": "feature-x",
  "profiles": {
    "feature-x": { "token": "redacted", "endpoint": "https://api.redwood.dev" }
  }
}
```
after (sanitized):
```
{
  "active_profile": "default",
  "profiles": {
    "default": { }
  }
}
```

alex: so it replaced the whole profiles map.

sophie: that confirms it. sounds like the updater writes a fresh default config and doesn't merge. we should never clobber existing profiles/tokens. high priority imo.

sam: adding context: we intentionally added a default-config write path in 1.3.0 to support first-run UX, but the updater should be using a merge strategy. looks like the updater code path calls writeDefaultConfig() without checking for an existing config file.

sam: quick mitigation we can ship: 1) update the updater to load existing config and deep-merge defaults (preserve existing keys), 2) make updater no-op on active_profile if it already exists, and 3) ensure backup of config before writing so localserve can recover on failure.

sophie: also: localserve should watch for profile changes but not immediately drop to login if tokens are present in disk. e.g. detect if active_profile changed but token exists -> continue serving and log a warning instead of forcing interactive login. that will reduce chatter during updates.

devex-bot: Filing: created issue #1512 (cli: updater clobbers ~/.config/redwood/config.json on update; breaks active_profile) and added label: autoupdate, high-priority

qa-bot: I can add a regression test to the updater pipeline that copies a sample config (with profile+token), runs the update flow, and asserts the profiles map still contains the original profile. assigning to @sam.

sam: thanks @qa-bot. I'll draft the PR with merge logic and a config backup step. linking initial branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cli/pull/1540

alex: appreciate it. small doc ask: can we add a note in release notes and troubleshooting about the updater's behavior and how to manually recover (copy ~/.config/redwood/config.json.bak back to config.json)? I lost ~10 minutes debugging this.

sophie: yes, add recovery steps to docs + consider adding a --no-auto-update flag for localdev mode.

sam: agreed on --no-auto-update; will add to PR. thanks for the report, alex. :thumbsup:
